Given that the point $A$ has coordinates $(-\sqrt{3},-1),$ calculate the angle $\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
We can form a triangle by creating a vertical line from $A$ to the $x$-axis. Let us call ${\theta }^{′}$ the acute angle that is formed with the $x$-axis such that ${\theta }^{′}+{180}^{∘}=\theta $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/d14f62179f831ebdc177eac7bd2899679864305d4104d4b61f304eb4fa9e133d.png)

Using the tangent ratio, we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{\theta }^{′}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$

Finally, using the inverse tangent, we get

$$
{\theta }^{′}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}={30}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, using $\theta ={\theta }^{′}+{180}^{∘},$ we get $\theta ={30}^{∘}+{180}^{∘}={210}^{∘}.$
